note: The English Wikipedia article says Quri Winchus holds remains of circular buildings of the Wanka period, but a period word alone gives no year, century or millennium for the site's start, so nothing dates it.

English and Spanish Wikipedia and the MINCETUR inventory record (cod_Ficha=4758) place Chichakuri (Chichacori, Ollachea, Puno) only in pre-Hispanic Colla times, a period word without a year, century or millennium; no source dates its start.

No page found prints a point for the Margarita Tomb itself; Wikipedia, Wikidata, Commons, Penn Museum, Florida Museum and Mesoweb give none, and the only printed point is for the whole Copan site, not the tomb.

No readable page prints coordinates for this tomb; the Megalithic Portal page returns 403 to a plain GET. The INAH salvage report places the tomb on the road to La Florida in the municipality of Valparaiso, while the stored point lies roughly 140 km from the La Florida hamlet of Valparaiso (OSM 22.68, -103.60), so the stored point cannot be vouched for.

The only article on this tomb gives 'two centuries before our era and 400 after Christ's' for the societies of the area in general and says the chamber was unaltered for at least 1,600 years; that is a regional range, not a stated start of this tomb.

No readable page prints a coordinate pair for the Keno Daas carvings: the Wikipedia article carries a coord-missing notice, Wikidata has no P625, and the Commons category and tourism pages give no point.
Prassa's sources (Wikipedia, minoancrete.com) date the houses only by Minoan phases (MM I to LM IA) without a year, century or millennium; no quotable date.
Askeladden gives only Stone Age (shoreline-dated, probable); Arild Hauge's text and Wikipedia say only hunting culture; no source gives a year.

The English Wikipedia article prints no coordinates, its Wikidata item (Q30588188) has no coordinate statement, and no readable page found prints a point for the burial site (the road Ny Gjellerupvej lies about 9.05 E, the stored point is in Herning itself).

The sources date the parish's remains only by period words - Bronze Age chambered cairns, about 60 Iron Age burial sites, five Iron Age hill forts, a dozen runic inscriptions; none gives a year, century or millennium for the start of the record.

The sources describe many kinds of remains at once (chambered cairns, around 60 burial sites, a tumulus, five hill forts, runic inscriptions), so no single canonical type holds, and no source states such a type word for the parish as a whole.

The Cultural Inventory record for Belören Kalesi, the only page I could read for this site, gives its name, type, status and region but prints no coordinates in its visible text, and I found no other readable source quoting a point for the castle. The stored point stays and the site goes to the owner's list.

The only dating I found for Belören Kalesi is Miras Haritası supposing a construction between the 5th and 1st centuries BC, a range for the monument's fabric rather than a stated year, century or millennium for its start. The empty field stays empty.

Wikipedia only says the main temple is of a style typical of the Postclassic (c. 950-1539 AD) in the Guatemalan Highlands, a stylistic range for a class of architecture, not a date for the start of this site; no readable source dates its start.
No readable page prints a point for the Tanjung Raja megalith complex in Gumay Ulu, Lahat; the national tourism register entry only links to Google Maps without printing coordinates.
No source found dates the Tanjung Raja megalith complex itself; pages on the Pasemah megaliths speak of the region in general.

The only page naming the site, the Sisparnas register entry 'Situs Megalit Tanjung Raja', gives just that Indonesian name; no readable page about this complex carries the word 'megalith' or states any other type.

No source prints a point for the Nakhchivan necropolises: the English and Azerbaijani Wikipedia articles give none, the Wikidata item has no coordinate, and no register or paper found places them; the stored point is only the city.
Wikipedia marks the coordinates as missing and Wikidata has no P625; no readable source found gives a point for Llaqta Qulluy in Tayacaja.
No readable source dates Llaqta Qulluy in Tayacaja; Wikipedia only gives the name's meaning.

The park is a group of eight sites (Li Muri, Li Lolghi, Albucciu, Moru, Malchittu, La Prisgiona, Coddu Vecchju and others) spread over the Arzachena area; the pages give a point only for single monuments (e.g. Wikipedia for Li Muri), none for the park itself.

Italia.it dates the park's eight sites only as a span from the 5th to the 2nd millennium BC, which does not state a start of its own in a form that can be quoted; the other pages date single monuments (Li Muri to the second half of the fourth millennium BC), not the park, so no source dates the start of the park itself.
The Rodadero is a natural diorite outcrop; no readable source gives a date for the start of its use as a site (the Spanish Wikipedia article on Suchuna and the travel pages give none).

Only Wikipedia/Wikidata print a point (15 14 28 S 70 16 40 W), and they print it for the mountain; SRTM gives about 4,198 m there against a 4,300 m peak that Arkush says the hillfort occupies, and the OpenStreetMap peak node lies 1.25 km west at the summit, so no quotable source gives the site's own point.

No readable source dates the construction of the Lupanar at VII.12.18-20; English, German, French, Italian Wikipedia, Pompeii Online and pompei.it give only the 1862 discovery, the 72 AD renovation (German) and the 79 AD eruption, none a start date.

English Wikipedia and Wikidata print no coordinates for Khichuqaqa (only Urubamba District, Cusco Region, on the slope of Kapuliyuq); the Hostnig rock-art survey cited there cannot be read by plain GET, and no readable source gives a point.
No readable source gives a year, century or millennium for Khichuqaqa; Wikipedia only says it is an archaeological site with rock paintings and tombs, undated.

Wikipedia says the age and purpose of the tracks are uncertain, with origins estimated from the Neolithic to Medieval times; a no-later-than c. 700 BC limit and a Temple Period range for several examples are ranges for the ruts, not a start year for the site, so no source dates its start.

The Via Militaris is a road of 924 km from Singidunum to Constantinople; neither its English article nor the Wikidata item Q1231059 prints a coordinate for the road, and no source point for it can be quoted, so the stored point stays.
the new point lies in [], the site says Cyprus

No source I could read quotes a point for Thigibba at Hammam Zouakra: the French Wikipedia article leaves its latitude and longitude fields empty and the Wikidata item Q104587876 for the site carries no coordinate statement, so nothing can be quoted and the stored point stays.

ISMEO/LoRAP's page gives the point of the Khao Sai On dioritic inselberg and, separately, points for the single excavation loci Khok Din and Noen Din, but no source states a point for the archaeological site as a whole, and the inselberg figure is the hill the site stands on, which this field excludes. The stored point lies about 8 km west of it, but nothing quotable fixes the site itself.

No source states a year, century or millennium for the start of Wila Wilani (Tacna). The English article gives no date at all, and the Spanish article's only figure, "Las pinturas están datadas de 7.000 años a. C.", is an age worked backwards from the present rather than a stated date, and it is flagged [ cita requerida ]. Neither is readable as a start year, so the field stays empty.

No readable page prints a point for the Mnemata Site / Agios Georgios cemetery of Kition: Wikipedia and Wikidata carry none, and the sources only describe it as 700 m north-west of the Kition city wall, so the stored point stays unconfirmed.

Wikipedia only says the site was a cemetery 'from the beginning of the Iron Age until the Roman times', a period word without a year, century or millennium, and the Hadjisavvas volumes that could date the first tombs are not readable.

The Fortifications of London are a system of walls, gates and forts across the city; the Wikipedia article and its Wikidata item carry no coordinates and no source gives one point for the system as a whole.
The sources about the Sahneh rock tombs give only period words (Median or Achaemenid; Persian Wikipedia's infobox gives the 1st millennium BC in Persian only), no English-readable dated start.
The only pages found about the rock tomb of Sahneh (Persian Wikipedia, visitiran.ir) never name it 'Tomb of the Scene', so no quote can name the site as required.
No readable source prints a coordinate pair for Nyaung-gan; Wikipedia carries no coordinates and Oakaie paper only says 35 km NNW of Monywa, which is not a point.
Wikipedia gives no date for Nyaung-gan itself (only Bronze Age); the literature gives only a range of estimates from the early-mid 2nd to the early-mid 1st millennium BC, not a start date.
